skill.name: hypothesis-generation
skill.description: Generate testable scientific hypotheses from observations, literature, and competing explanations. Design experiments, predictions, quality checks, and formatted research reports.
skill.summary: Structured support for evidence-based hypothesis generation and experimental planning.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code spans, PubMed example URLs, and research-writing guidance. Two external command blocks are confirmed, and contextual review found mandatory external schematic generation plus privacy exposure from web literature searches. No prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Make command execution optional, require user confirmation, and document the trusted source and expected path for scripts/generate_schematic.py.
Tell users to review generated .tex and .bib files before running XeLaTeX or BibTeX, and avoid shell escape.
Disclose the scientific-schematics and Nano Banana Pro dependency, make it opt-in, and warn before sending unpublished research details.
Ask users before WebFetch or WebSearch calls and advise them to remove sensitive unpublished terms from search queries.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md requires every report to include AI-generated figures using the scientific-schematics skill and Nano Banana Pro. This introduces an unaudited dependency and possible third-party processing of research details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dependency is explicitly mandatory in the skill instructions. The security impact depends on the external skill and service behavior, which are not included in this package.

content.value_statement: Researchers need structured hypotheses that connect observations, literature, and experiments. This skill guides hypothesis creation, quality checks, predictions, and report formatting.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through clarifying observations, scope, constraints, and relevant scientific domains.
Provides literature search strategies for PubMed and broader scientific sources.
Generates three to five competing mechanistic hypotheses from evidence and observations.
Evaluates hypotheses for testability, falsifiability, parsimony, explanatory power, and novelty.
Proposes experiments, controls, confounds, measurements, and testable predictions.
Structures a concise LaTeX hypothesis report with appendices and bibliography guidance.
limitations: It does not prove that a hypothesis is true or ready for publication.
It depends on the quality and completeness of the literature and user-provided context.
External searches can expose sensitive research topics unless users review queries first.
LaTeX compilation and schematic generation may require local tools or external services.

use_cases.title: Plan a Thesis Experiment
use_cases.description: Turn a research observation into competing hypotheses, predictions, controls, and first-pass experimental designs.

use_cases.title: Compare Mechanistic Explanations
use_cases.description: Organize evidence for several mechanisms and identify experiments that distinguish between them.

use_cases.title: Draft a Research Brief
use_cases.description: Create a structured hypothesis report with summary, key evidence, predictions, and detailed appendices.

prompt_templates.title: Start From an Observation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill. My observation is: [describe observation]. Generate three testable hypotheses with one prediction each.

prompt_templates.title: Add Literature Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with known papers or findings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill. Given these findings: [summarize evidence], create competing mechanisms and note what literature would support each one.

prompt_templates.title: Design Discriminating Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill. Compare these hypotheses: [list hypotheses]. Propose experiments, controls, confounds, and falsifying results for each one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Full Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a structured research deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill to produce a concise hypothesis report for [topic]. Include competing hypotheses, predictions, experiments, quality assessment, and appendices.

output_examples.input: Observation: A treatment improves recovery in young mice but has little effect in old mice.
output: Hypothesis 1: Age-related immune remodeling reduces treatment response.
Prediction: Treated old mice will show weaker inflammatory resolution markers than treated young mice.
Experiment: Compare immune cell profiles across treated and control groups at early and late time points.

output_examples.input: Request: Compare two mechanisms for a climate feedback pattern.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate each mechanism, list supporting evidence, define distinguishing predictions, and propose observations that could falsify each explanation.

output_examples.input: Request: Turn a literature gap into a report outline for a grant planning meeting.
output: Executive summary with the central phenomenon and strongest uncertainty.
Competing hypotheses with evidence, assumptions, and predicted outcomes.
Appendix plan for literature review, experimental methods, and quality assessment.

best_practices: Provide the observation, domain, constraints, known evidence, and excluded explanations before asking for hypotheses.
Review search queries before external literature searches, especially for unpublished or proprietary research.
Ask for falsifying predictions and controls, not only supportive evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated hypotheses as validated scientific conclusions.
Do not request only one favored explanation when competing hypotheses are needed.
Do not compile generated LaTeX or run helper scripts without reviewing the files first.

faq.question: Does this skill replace expert scientific review?
faq.answer: No. It supports scientific reasoning, but claims still need expert review and empirical testing.

faq.question: Can it work outside biomedical research?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow applies across domains, but PubMed examples are most useful for biomedical topics.

faq.question: Does it search the literature automatically?
faq.answer: It gives search guidance and may use web tools when available. Users should review sensitive queries first.

faq.question: What output format does it prefer?
faq.answer: It emphasizes a concise LaTeX report with main text, appendices, citations, and formatted hypothesis boxes.

faq.question: How many hypotheses does it generate?
faq.answer: The workflow recommends three to five competing hypotheses for a balanced comparison.

faq.question: Can it design experiments?
faq.answer: Yes. It proposes measurements, controls, confounds, study designs, and predictions for each hypothesis.
